topic: Unlocking the Geometry of Networks: Planar Graphs and Euler’s Formula
target_audience: University students (Computer Science or Mathematics majors)

sections.title: Introduction: The Map-Maker's Challenge
lecture_lines: A planar graph has no crossing edges.
We can redraw graphs to remove crossings.
This is vital for subway map design.
animations: Fade in text 'The Map-Maker's Challenge' #FFFFFF in center.
Fade out text, draw a simple planar map #FF0000.
Highlight vertices of the map in #00FF00.
Highlight edges connecting the vertices in #0000FF.
Fill faces of the map with light grey #CCCCCC.

sections.title: Core Components: Vertices, Edges, and Faces
lecture_lines: Graphs consist of vertices and edges.
The infinite area is a face.

sections.title: Euler’s Characteristic Formula
lecture_lines: Euler’s formula relates V, E, and F.
V minus E plus F equals 2.
This constant holds for planar graphs.
Check it with a simple square.
The formula remains true regardless of complexity.
animations: Flash V, E, F in colors #00FF00, #0000FF, #FF0000.
Scale up equation to center screen.

sections.title: The Concept of Dual Graphs
lecture_lines: Dual graphs are created from faces.
Place a vertex in each face.
animations: Fade in dual graph G* in #FF0000.
Show correspondence between faces and vertices.

sections.title: Summary & Application
lecture_lines: It is essential for graph coloring.
